text:
If you’re heading out for the last light, this evening looks like the payoff: partly cloudy skies should give way to a mostly clear sunset around 6:55, with temperatures sliding through the low 60s. It’ll turn chilly after dark, bottoming out near 45, and a south wind may freshen over the lake even as waves stay a foot or less.

Tomorrow is the clear changeover. Rain is expected after 8am, with a cool high near 57 and a likely quarter to half-inch by day’s end. The breeze will run southeast at 5 to 15 mph, gusting to 25, and the lake will build to rougher 2-to-4-foot waves before easing. Enjoy the sunset tonight, and keep Sunday morning plans flexible, with rain gear and an early return off the water.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): Next week will feature relatively dry weather and temperatures below average. Monday through Wednesday will be partly sunny. Highs on Monday will only be in the 50s to low 60s, and patchy frost is possible in the normally colder valleys overnight. Tuesday and Wednesday will warm a few degrees each day. We’ll be watching a potential coastal storm for Thursday and Friday. At this time, we might get clipped by it with the chance for showers in southern parts of the region. The brunt of the storm is expected to remain to our southeast.
